claim: In KOMBINE, finding the shared abstraction (generic space) is the bottleneck for LLM blending, not building the blend (coherent blend 97.1% given a valid generic space); separately, AnaloBench finds retrieving an analogous story from a large bank is near random for long stories. Whether the retrieval or the abstraction step is the harder one for distant-domain sources was not tested directly.
agent_test: Same token budget: (A) direct combine of two given concepts vs (B) first spend tokens on extracting a shared abstraction then combine; measure valid-blend rate.
audit_note: KOMBINE does report an abstraction bottleneck (blends coherent 97.1% given a valid generic space), but its tasks give the model both inputs, so it does not test retrieval of distant-domain sources; AnaloBench shows retrieval from a bank is hard but does not isolate abstraction from retrieval.
claim_before_audit: Retrieval of distant-domain sources, abstracted to a shared principle, is the hard step for LLMs: finding the shared abstraction (blend generic space) is the bottleneck, not building the blend.

claim: Given a valid shared abstraction, LLMs build a coherent blend almost always (97.1%).
agent_test: Inject a supplied generic space and check blend coherence; if ~97% holds, spend tokens on abstraction search only.

claim: LLMs are weak at retrieving analogues from a large bank, near random for long stories and big banks; human-LLM gap grows from 6.9 to 28.8 points as stories lengthen.
agent_test: Test retrieval of analogues from a memory bank with abstraction-level keys vs surface keys at equal tokens.
audit_note: AnaloBench confirmed (340 analogies, GPT-4 human gap 6.9 to 28.8 points, near-random on long stories/large bank); gap is for GPT-4 specifically and 2024 models; ARN (far analogies below random) is consistent.

claim: GPT-3's zero-shot analogy ability does not generalise: counterfactual alphabets cut accuracy sharply while humans stay steady; claims of emergent analogy are contested.
schema_part: G (do not trust self-reported analogy success)
agent_test: Evaluate the agent on counterfactual/permuted variants of its own analogy tasks; require invariance.

claim: Story (causal, cross-domain) analogies are where GPT-3 is clearly worse than humans, and far analogy is not above chance for it.
agent_test: Check far-analogy transfer separately from near; report both.
audit_note: Webb text verified (GPT-3 near analogy p=0.0039, far analogy p=0.065 not significant, human advantage OR=0.37); 'not above chance' means not statistically significant, and results are GPT-3 only.

claim: Distance alone does not predict success in human field data (chi2=0.00, p=.92); iteration on distant-sourced ideas helps (+0.45 log-odds per 0.10, p=.07 marginal).
agent_test: Compare one-shot far combination vs 2-4 iterations at equal tokens, scoring after each pass.

claim: Lab studies agree far combinations raise novelty but give mixed or lower quality.
agent_test: Vary source distance; score novelty and validity separately.

claim: Far-source analogy retrieval by purpose and mechanism raised the share of good human ideas (0.71 vs 0.28 TF-IDF, k=2; 0.56 vs 0.16, k=3). A same-group 2022 follow-up with a learned extractor found 51% useful inspirations vs under 30% for the best baseline (not independent).
agent_test: Index memory by purpose and mechanism, not surface text; compare against embedding-of-text retrieval.

claim: Retrieval-augmented LLM ideation yields higher blind-rated novelty than experts (5.64 vs 4.84) but not better feasibility or overall.
agent_test: Rate novelty and feasibility separately; do not select on novelty alone.

claim: The novelty edge of LLM ideas vanishes when ideas are executed (novelty change -1.049 vs -0.010; overall -1.976 vs -0.628).
agent_test: Execute or test the generated idea (code/check) before accepting; compare accept-on-novelty vs accept-after-test.

claim: Mass LLM idea generation hits a duplicate wall: 4000 ideas yield about 200 non-duplicates (cos>0.8).
agent_test: Measure unique-idea yield per token; use seed conditioning or forced-different-source prompts.

claim: LLMs converge: different models and repeated samples produce the same ideas (19.9% of invented concepts share 2 properties; response similarity >0.8 in the Hivemind study).
agent_test: Force sampling from different source domains per branch; measure pairwise similarity at equal tokens.
audit_note: KOMBINE 19.9% (412/2,070) share at least 2 near-identical properties and Hivemind pairwise similarity typically above 0.8 both verified; 'same ideas' means near-identical, and similarity metrics differ between studies.

claim: LLM judges are unreliable for idea quality: the best LLM evaluator reached 53.3% agreement on idea ranking, below expert inter-reviewer consistency of 56.1% (Si et al. 2024; the 71.4% figure is for accepted-vs-rejected ICLR paper prediction), and LLM-human Pearson r on research-ideation contribution is only 0.159 (best 0.234) (arXiv 2508.05470).
agent_test: Do not use the same model as sole judge of combination value; use external checks.
audit_note: 71.4% is zero-shot accuracy on picking the accepted ICLR paper of an accepted/rejected pair, not idea-quality judging; the 56.1% is human inter-reviewer consistency on ideas, where the best LLM judge (Claude-3.5 pairwise ranker) got only 53.3%, so the pair of numbers is not comparable.
claim_before_audit: LLM judges are unreliable for creativity/idea quality (best 71.4% pairwise vs human 56.1%; LLM-human r=0.159 on contribution).

claim: Word-level far association (DAT) is a weak proxy: GPT-4 beats human mean but top human decile wins and outputs are repetitive.
agent_test: Do not use DAT as a success measure for O7.

claim: Self-generated analogical exemplars give small gains on reasoning (+1 to +3 points GSM8K/MATH, GPT-3.5), but sources are near, not distant.
agent_test: Self-recall of related problems before solving, equal tokens vs plain CoT.

claim: Users tend to ignore far facets even when offered; participants used input and near facets far more.
agent_test: Check the agent actually uses far candidates; log usage.

claim: Facet-based decomposition (purpose, mechanism, evaluation) improves overlap detection with prior work (89.66% vs under 14%) and recombination support.
agent_test: Decompose-then-recombine vs holistic prompt; check novelty against known prior work.

claim: Gu et al. 2025: abstraction-level retrieval raises similarity of output to the true paper idea (0.85 vs 0.78), but baseline lacks the references, no judge, no ablation, no variance.
agent_test: Re-run with equal knowledge base given to baseline; ablate abstraction levels.

claim: Information about who works on what (human-aware models) improves discovery prediction up to 400%, and atypical but mostly conventional combinations get most impact.
agent_test: Not testable on our agent directly; treat as background.

claim: Combinational creativity as link prediction on concept graphs is a workable framing, but popularity bias dominates.
agent_test: Not tested at equal tokens; low priority.

claim: Chatbots out-score humans on the Alternate Uses Task on mean, but human deficit shrinks on max scores with time and instruction.
agent_test: Compare max-of-k not mean.

claim: Few-shot examples pull LLM design ideas toward the crowd solutions (less novel).
agent_test: Test example-free vs example-seeded generation for diversity.

claim: Uzzi et al. 2013 (read): top-5% citation hit rate is 9.11 per 100 for papers with high median conventionality plus high tail novelty, vs 5 background, 5.82 conventional-only, 5.33 novel-only, 2.05 for neither. Best impact comes from a conventional base with a small atypical insert.
agent_test: Compare all-far, all-near and mostly-near plus one far source on an executable check.

claim: LLM analogy skill is brittle under counterfactual and paraphrase variants for GPT-3/3.5/4 while humans hold steady; no Claude-class or reasoning-model test was found.
agent_test: Run the mapping step on counterfactual and order-swapped items before use.

claim: Far narrative analogy detection: models average 39.6% (below the 50% chance level) vs humans 94.1%; GPT-4 is below random on far items while near to human on near items.
agent_test: Do not let the model alone judge far analogy; require an executable check.

claim: Iterated planned retrieval raises unique novel ideas (3.4x in Nova) and gains stop after about 3 rounds; but the study does not vary distance and is not at equal tokens.
agent_test: Compare 1, 2, 3, 4 rounds at fixed token budget on a code task with tests.

claim: For executable tasks, archive-based recombination beats repeated fresh sampling at equal compute (AlphaEvolve ablation 'no evolution'), and a cheap embedding filter for near-duplicates raises score (ShinkaEvolve). Neither isolates source distance.
agent_test: Use execution score as the validity check; add a duplicate filter.
audit_note: AlphaEvolve ablation is repeated feeding of the same initial program vs evolutionary database (figure-only); 'recombination' and 'equal compute' are slight paraphrases.

claim: Gaps 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 (LLM-agent form), 9 (Claude and reasoning models) and 10 have no direct study found; distance, abstraction-first and source forcing at equal tokens remain untested.
agent_test: Run an own ablation: none / near / far sources at equal tokens, scored by unit tests.

claim: Structured organisation of retrieved sources (chain, entities) matters more than mere inclusion in LLM-judged ablations; judge is an LLM so weak.
agent_test: Ablate ordered vs unordered sources with an execution score.
